### Mongoose layer bleed in resolver: isValidObjectId guard and ImpersonationRequestModel type (ADR 018)

**Suggestion Severity**

The new `findRequestOrNull` helper imports `isValidObjectId` from 'mongoose' and annotates its return as `ImpersonationRequestModel | null`, putting Mongoose-level identifier validation and the persistence type into the resolver/transport layer. ADR 018's layering states resolvers consume DTOs while models never leave the repository/service layer; the sibling audit service shows the correct home for this guard (it uses `isValidObjectId` inside the service).

**Fix:**
```
Move the invalid-ObjectId check into ImpersonationRequestService.findById so an invalid id translates to ImpersonationRequestNotFoundError (or a null contract); the resolver then keeps its existing try/catch on the domain error and needs no direct 'mongoose' import or ImpersonationRequestModel annotation.
```

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Fixed. The ObjectId guard now lives in `ImpersonationRequestService.findById`, which throws `ImpersonationRequestNotFoundError` for an invalid id without querying Mongo (new unit test in `impersonation-request.service.unit.test.ts`). The resolver no longer imports `mongoose` and no longer annotates the model type.

### Enum registration moved out of its definition file, breaking the impersonation module pattern

**Suggestion Severity**

Every other impersonation enum (ImpersonationRequestStatusEnum, ImpersonationTargetAppEnum, ImpersonationAuditEventTypeEnum) calls registerEnumType in its own enum file under domains/enums/. The new ImpersonationConsentAccessEnum instead registers from the outputDto, so the enum file (impersonation-consent-access.enum.ts) is not self-registering like its siblings; a future second registration site would crash Nest's boot with a duplicate-name error.

**Fix:**
```
Move registerEnumType(ImpersonationConsentAccessEnum, { name: 'ImpersonationConsentAccessEnum' }) into domains/enums/impersonation-consent-access.enum.ts and remove it (and the registerEnumType import) from impersonation-consent.output.dto.ts.
```

comments.body:

### New neighbour unit test hand-rolls mock scaffolding instead of Suites TestBed.solitary() (ADR 031 §16)

**Suggestion Severity**

ADR 031 §16 (superseding ADR 008) requires every `*.unit.test.ts` outside `cells/` to use `TestBed.solitary(ServiceUnderTest).compile()` with `unitRef.get<T>(T)` typed mocks, explicitly rejecting hand-rolled scaffolding because it drifts with constructor changes and relies on `as unknown as` casts. This new file builds the `ImpersonationAuditService` with `new` and casts every collaborator (`dataService as unknown as IDataServices`, `logger as unknown as Logger`). The sibling impersonation tests follow the same hand-rolled pattern, so this may be an established directory lane predating the ADR.

**Fix:**
```
Migrate the suite to `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationAuditService).compile()` and retrieve typed mocks via `unitRef.get(IDataServices)` / `unitRef.get(Logger)`, keeping the existing `it.each` cases and assertions unchanged.
```

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Fixed. The suite now builds `ImpersonationAuditService` with `TestBed.solitary(...).compile()` and `unitRef.get<T>(T)` (with `@ts-expect-error` on the `IDataServices` token, as §16 requires). Returned documents are typed `mockDeep<Model>()` instances, so no `as unknown as` cast remains.

### New neighbour resolver unit test bypasses the Suites TestBed.solitary() container (ADR 031 §16)

**Suggestion Severity**

ADR 031 §16 mandates `TestBed.solitary()` with `unitRef.get<T>(T)` for neighbour `*.unit.test.ts` files. This new suite constructs `ImpersonationHostResolver` directly with manually built stub objects (`requestService = { findById: vi.fn() }`, `dataServices as unknown as IDataServices`), which will silently miss newly injected constructor dependencies. Behaviour, naming (`should <X> when <Y>`), and AAA structure otherwise match the ADR.

**Fix:**
```
Rebuild with `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationHostResolver).compile()` and retrieve mocks for `ImpersonationRequestService`, `ImpersonationAuditService`, `PosthogService` and `IDataServices` via `unitRef.get`, preserving the existing test cases.
```

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Fixed. The resolver suite now uses `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationHostResolver).compile()` and gets `ImpersonationRequestService`, `ImpersonationAuditService`, `PosthogService` and `IDataServices` through `unitRef.get<T>(T)`. The request and context fixtures are typed `mockDeep` instances.

<!-- ai-review: {"title":"Hardcoded colors instead of design-system theme tokens","severity":"suggestion","category":"i18n"} -->
### Hardcoded colors instead of design-system theme tokens

**Suggestion Severity**

The new card uses raw Tailwind palette classes (bg-gray-50, bg-white, bg-amber-50, text-amber-600) and a hardcoded rgba shadow (rgba(16,31,52,0.1)) instead of theme variables. Other surfaces in the component correctly use tokens (bg-background, text-foreground, border-border), so these bypass the design system and break dark mode / theme overrides.

**Fix:**
```
Replace bg-gray-50 with bg-muted (or bg-background), bg-white with bg-card, bg-amber-50/text-amber-600 with the DS warning tokens (e.g. bg-warning-muted / text-warning), and use the shadow-sm/shadow-card token instead of the literal rgba value.
```

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body:
Fixed for the card: `bg-background`, `bg-warning-background`, `text-warning` and `shadow-sm` replace the raw palette and the rgba shadow. They render the same values in the default theme; under `data-ds-theme="2026"` the card now follows that theme's `--background` (#fdfdfd) instead of hard white, which is the point of the token. The page background stays `bg-gray-50`: no semantic token maps to gray-50 (`muted` is gray-100), and the sibling consent screens use the same page background.

https://github.com/naboo-team/naboo/blob/64732566c3401100ae3e766155ee98e946180f41/packages/tailwind-config/variables.css#L23-L36

comments.author: chrispop22
comments.body:
The resolver is built with `new` and hand-rolled collaborators cast with `as unknown as …`, three of which are empty `{} as …` stubs. ADR 031 §16 says: "Neighbour units are solitary and use Suites `TestBed.solitary(X).compile()` with `unitRef.get<T>(T)`, never hand-rolled mocks".
Impact: the mocks are no longer type-checked against the real dependencies, so a constructor change can leave this test green with the wrong wiring.
Suggestion: build it with `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationAdminResolver).compile()` and get each collaborator through `unitRef.get<T>(T)`.

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Fixed. The resolver is now built with `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationAdminResolver).compile()`, and each collaborator comes from `unitRef.get<T>(T)`. The admin, context and created request are typed `mockDeep` instances, so no hand-rolled `{} as ...` stub remains.

comments.author: chrispop22
comments.body:
The service is built with `new` and a hand-rolled `dataService as unknown as IDataServices`. ADR 031 §16 requires `TestBed.solitary(X).compile()` with `unitRef.get<T>(T)` for neighbour units.
Impact: the mocks are no longer type-checked against the real dependencies.
Suggestion: use `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationRequestService).compile()`. `IDataServices` is an abstract DI token, so per the ADR put `@ts-expect-error` on its `unitRef.get` line.

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Fixed. The service is built with `TestBed.solitary(ImpersonationRequestService).compile()`, and `IDataServices` comes from `unitRef.get` with `@ts-expect-error` on that line, as the ADR says.

comments.author: chrispop22
comments.body:
No test checks that `clientRequestId` reaches the `createImpersonationRequest` variables. The prop is optional, so removing it at the `ClientRequestImpersonationTab` call site, or removing this line, still typechecks.
Impact: requests would be created without a link, `impersonation-audit.service.ts:136` would return early without logging anything, and the client request Activities tab would be empty again (the SEC2-198 defect) while every test stays green.
Suggestion: render `ImpersonationRequestForm` with `clientRequestId="cr-1"` and a mocked mutation, submit, and assert `dto.clientRequestId === "cr-1"`. Add a second case with no prop that asserts it is undefined.

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Good catch, fixed with two tests. `ImpersonationRequestForm.unit.test.tsx` renders the form with `clientRequestId`, submits it and asserts the exact `dto` sent to the mutation, plus a case without the prop that asserts it is undefined. `ClientRequestImpersonationTab.unit.test.tsx` asserts the tab passes `clientRequestId` to the form. I checked that removing either the prop at the tab call site or the line in `handleSubmit` turns a test red.

comments.author: chrispop22
comments.body:
`req-close-twice` is not an ObjectId, so `writeClientRequestLog` returns at the `isValidObjectId` guard, both here and in every other boot case. The title says "skip the feed entry", but only `endReason` is asserted. Outside the mocked unit tests, nothing exercises the feed write against real Mongo.
Impact: if the `clientRequestId` `@Prop` is lost, Mongoose strict mode strips it silently. If the `impersonation` subdocument is rejected (its `requestId` is required), the catch only logs it. In both cases the Activities feed stays empty and CI stays green.
Suggestion: in this suite, create a real impersonation request with an ObjectId `clientRequestId`, call `logEvent(REQUEST_CREATED)`, and assert that one `logs` document exists with type `IMPERSONATION_REQUEST_CREATED`, the matching `clientRequestId` and `impersonation.requestId`. For this close-twice case, use a real linked request and assert exactly one `IMPERSONATION_SESSION_ENDED` log.

comments.author: sarah-bourgeois
comments.body: Good catch, fixed. The boot suite now creates a real impersonation request with an ObjectId `clientRequestId`, calls `logEvent(REQUEST_CREATED)` and asserts one `logs` document with the type, the `clientRequestId` and `impersonation.requestId`. The close-twice case now uses a linked request and asserts a single `IMPERSONATION_SESSION_ENDED` entry. I checked that removing the `clientRequestId` `@Prop` makes both tests fail.

### Hardcoded palette color instead of semantic design token

**Suggestion Severity**

The page background uses `bg-gray-50`, a raw palette color, while the rest of the component correctly uses semantic tokens (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `border-border`). This bypasses the design system's theme variables and won't adapt if a semantic surface token changes.

**Fix:**
```
Replace `bg-gray-50` with the semantic surface token, e.g. `bg-muted` (or whatever token the DS defines for page backgrounds).
```

Keeping `bg-gray-50` on purpose. No semantic token maps to gray-50: `--muted` is gray-100, so `bg-muted` would darken the page, and there is no page-surface token in the shared config.

https://github.com/naboo-team/naboo/blob/1df6d9bd90bf58c1504c11939d225dbe79db55bc/packages/tailwind-config/variables.css#L23-L36

The sibling consent screens use the same page background, so switching only this one would make the consent flow inconsistent:

https://github.com/naboo-team/naboo/blob/1df6d9bd90bf58c1504c11939d225dbe79db55bc/packages/app-host/app/%5Blocale%5D/impersonation/consent/_components/ConsentPageContent.tsx#L53-L55

comments.author: linear[bot]
comments.body:
SEC2-198 Impersonation audit trail — confirm visibility in main client activity log

## Context During live testing on PR-14550, no impersonation action (request created, cancelled, expired) appeared in the client record's general "Activités" tab — only in the dedicated Impersonation "Historique des demandes" table. ## Scope Confirm with Sarah Bourgeois whether this is intended final behavior. If yes, assess whether isolated audit trail is sufficient for ISO 27001 / SOC 2 audit traceability requirements, or whether it should also surface in the main activity log. ## Status / decisions Sarah confirmed (Slack, 09/07): events are correctly stored in ActivityTracking (same collection, correct architecture), but the BO only surfaces them in the dedicated Impersonation tab, not in the general activity feed. **Decision: this is a blocking prerequisite for vCISO go/no-go on production release.** Rationale: audit trail for privileged support access must be discoverable in the main activity flow for ISO 27001 A.8.15 / SOC 2 CC7.2 traceability — an external auditor or client shouldn't need to be told to look in a separate tab. Fix does not need to be exhaustive/polished for go-live, just needs to make impersonation events visible in the main activity flow.

Review in Linear
